req.title: Reflect query parameters on GET
req.statement: The system shall include client-supplied query parameters under the 'args' key of the GET /get response body.
expected_outcomes: response args field mirrors query string

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /get must reflect client-supplied query parameters under the 'args' key. I designed tests covering: (1) a positive EP case with a single k=v pair asserting exact key and value; (2) a positive EP case with multiple parameters asserting all are reflected; (3) a negative path case with no query parameters asserting args is an empty dict (not None, not absent); (4) a BVA boundary case with an empty-string value for a key; (5) a DT case with special characters in values; (6) a NEG case verifying that args does NOT contain keys not sent. These tests assert exact values to kill constant-mutation, key-deletion, and dict-substitution mutants. The 'args' field is populated by semiflatten(request.args) in get_dict(), so mutations to that path will be caught by exact-value assertions.

tests.name: test_get_single_query_param_reflected_in_args
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send GET /get?foo=bar using Flask test client
trace: R-HTTPBIN-002: args key mirrors query string
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_get_single_query_param_reflected_in_args():
    r = client.get('/get?foo=bar')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert 'args' in body
    assert body['args'] == {'foo': 'bar'}
    assert len(body['args']) == 1

test_get_single_query_param_reflected_in_args()

tests.name: test_get_query_param_empty_string_value_boundary
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send GET /get?key= (key with empty string value) using Flask test client
expected: args['key'] == '' exactly (empty string, not None, not absent)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-002: boundary — empty string value must be reflected exactly
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_get_query_param_empty_string_value_boundary():
    r = client.get('/get?key=')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert 'args' in body
    assert 'key' in body['args']
    assert body['args']['key'] == ''

tests.name: test_get_args_does_not_contain_unsent_keys
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send GET /get?only=this using Flask test client
expected: args contains exactly one key 'only' with value 'this'
args does NOT contain keys 'other', 'extra', or any other key
trace: R-HTTPBIN-002: args must mirror only the supplied query string, no phantom keys
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_get_args_does_not_contain_unsent_keys():
    r = client.get('/get?only=this')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert 'args' in body
    assert body['args'] == {'only': 'this'}
    assert 'other' not in body['args']
    assert 'extra' not in body['args']
    assert len(body['args']) == 1

test_get_args_does_not_contain_unsent_keys()

tests.name: test_get_special_characters_in_query_param_value
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send GET /get?msg=hello+world&sym=%21 using Flask test client
trace: R-HTTPBIN-002: args must reflect decoded query parameter values
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_get_special_characters_in_query_param_value():
    r = client.get('/get?msg=hello+world&sym=%21')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert 'args' in body
    assert body['args']['msg'] == 'hello world'
    assert body['args']['sym'] == '!'
    assert len(body['args']) == 2

tests.name: test_get_response_top_level_keys_include_args_url_headers_origin
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send GET /get?x=y using Flask test client
expected: Response body contains exactly the keys: url, args, headers, origin
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_get_response_top_level_keys_include_args_url_headers_origin():
    r = client.get('/get?x=y')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert set(body.keys()) == {'url', 'args', 'headers', 'origin'}
    assert body['args'] == {'x': 'y'}
    assert 'url' in body
    assert 'headers' in body
    assert 'origin' in body

test_get_response_top_level_keys_include_args_url_headers_origin()
